text: Hergé's The Adventures of Tintin in the Congo was moved to an area reserved for adult graphic novels by the bookseller Borders in July 2007, and Waterstone's followed suit. In 2007 the Brooklyn Public Library removed the book from public display and kept it locked in a back room. In August 2007 a student filed a complaint in Brussels demanding a ban. In September 2011 the book was removed from a children's library in Kulturhuset in Stockholm. In February 2012 the Brussels court ruled that the book would not be banned.
meta_description: Hergé's Tintin in the Congo: moved to adult sections in July 2007, removed in Brooklyn and Stockholm, and not banned by a Brussels court in February 2012.
changes: Chronological order; the Brussels complaint and ruling now bracket the other events.
